title: How To Protect Black Students From Teacher Racial Discrimination https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2020/07/04/black-students-teacher-racial-discrimination/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Citing research that Black students are disciplined more severely than white classmates for identical misbehavior, Linsin argues that the subjective, discretionary classroom management methods common in schools today — token economies, rewards, teacher-issued 'logical consequences' — create the conditions for that bias, while a rules-and-consequences plan built on objective, pre-taught criteria closes the gap. He walks through the mechanics: rules and consequences are modeled and fully understood in advance so behavior is either clearly broken or not; consequences are delivered unemotionally, like a referee calling a foul, rather than through lectures or scolding; enforcement is completely consistent regardless of who breaks the rule; and rewards and behavior contracts, which he says disproportionately target Black students and function as a form of labeling, are forbidden entirely. He frames this objective, referee-style structure as making any existing discrimination immediately visible and nearly impossible to hide, and closes with an offer to consult free of charge with any school or district that commits to the approach.
points: Objective, pre-taught rules and consequences remove the subjective discretion that research links to harsher discipline of Black students.
Consequences should be delivered unemotionally, like a referee calling a foul, never through lectures, scolding, or glaring.
Rules and consequences must be enforced with total consistency regardless of who breaks them, eliminating any appearance of favoritism.
Rewards and behavior contracts are forbidden under this approach because they disproportionately target and label Black students.
A fully objective, rules-based system makes any remaining discrimination by a teacher immediately visible and hard to hide.
quotes: Studies show that Black students are disciplined more severely than their White classmates for the same misbehavior.
Our approach protects Black students from being singled out, profiled, and punished more harshly because of the color of their skin.
Consequences are enforced by the teacher like a good referee calls a foul in a sports game. That is, a student is informed that they broke a rule unemotionally and with respect.
Teachers consistently enforce consequences whenever a rule is broken. Consistent means every single time regardless of who breaks a rule .

Behavior contracts, which are often directed at Black children, are forbidden. They’re a form of labeling that tell students (and their classmates) very clearly that they’re different, less than, and not good enough.
With SCM, any existing or future racial discrimination or classroom management bias becomes glaringly obvious to all stakeholders and nearly impossible to hide.
